newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall despite bank gains.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall despite bank gains.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange fell 0.27 percent on Tuesday despite strong gains by the heavily-traded Jordan National Bank.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index slipped 0.43 points to 156.74 points in turnover of 868,000 dinars ($1,225,000).

Jordan National Bank, which last month swallowed up The Business Bank in Jordan's first bank merger, defied the downward trend and continued a three-day rally to close at 2.07 dinars after trade worth just under 300,000 dinars.
It rose 0.10 dinars to 2.10 dinars at one stage before slipping back to 2.07 dinars.
"It seemed to hit an equilibrium at that level and there was a lot of trading," said analyst Mohamad Abdallah.
But other blue-chip stocks dropped on Tuesday as falling shares outnumbered gainers by 29 to five.
"It's just a correction after the market went up in the last few days," Abdallah said. "There's still interest from the institutional buyers."

Shares rose on Saturday to a 14-month high, boosted by a recent parliamentary decision to scrap a 15 percent tax on transfers of cash from reserves into paid-up capital. Brokers say foreign buying also propelled the official index higher.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.52 percent to 82.63 points.
